easy.question: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
easy.explanation: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: horizontal, vertical, and two diagonals.

easy.question: A shape with no line of symmetry is called ______.
easy.explanation: Asymmetrical means the shape cannot be divided into two matching halves.

easy.question: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
easy.explanation: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry: one horizontal and one vertical through its centre.

easy.question: A ______ has endless (infinite) lines of symmetry.
easy.explanation: Any line passing through the centre of a circle divides it into two matching halves.

medium.question: How can you test if a paper shape has symmetry?
medium.answer: Fold the shape along a line. If the two halves overlap exactly, the shape is symmetrical and the fold is the line of symmetry.
medium.explanation: The folding test is the simplest way to check for symmetry in paper shapes.

medium.question: Why is the word AMBULANCE printed backwards on the front of ambulances?
medium.answer: So that drivers ahead can read it correctly in their rear-view mirrors. A mirror reverses left and right, so the reversed word appears normal when viewed in the mirror.
medium.explanation: Rear-view mirrors flip the image. Printing the word backwards cancels out the flip, making it readable.

medium.question: Which English letter does NOT have symmetry?
medium.explanation: A has a vertical line of symmetry, O has multiple lines, H has both horizontal and vertical. G has no line of symmetry.

hard.question: Only the digits 0, 1, and 8 look the same in a mirror. List at least 5 three-digit numbers made from these digits that would look the same in a mirror.
hard.explanation: Numbers made only from the digits 0, 1, and 8 appear unchanged in a mirror because each of these digits is mirror-symmetrical.

easy.question: Which shape leaves gaps when you try to tile a surface with it?
easy.explanation: Circles have curved edges that always leave gaps between them.

easy.question: Tiling means covering a surface with no ______ and no ______.
easy.explanation: Perfect tiling fills the entire surface without empty spaces or tiles stacked on top of each other.

easy.question: If you fold a paper once and cut a shape along the fold, how many lines of symmetry does the result have?
easy.explanation: One fold creates one line of symmetry. The cut shape appears equally on both sides of the fold.

medium.question: Can a regular hexagon tile a surface? Can a regular pentagon? Explain the difference.
medium.answer: A hexagon can tile a surface — honeycombs are a natural example. A pentagon cannot tile because when you place pentagons side by side, they leave gaps. The angles of a hexagon add up nicely at meeting points (3 hexagons make 360 degrees), but pentagon angles do not.
medium.explanation: Tiling requires that shapes meet perfectly at each point with no leftover angles. Hexagons fit; pentagons do not.

medium.question: If you fold a sheet of paper twice and make one cut, how many copies of the cut shape will you see when you unfold?
medium.answer: 4 copies. Each fold doubles the layers. First fold gives 2 layers, second fold gives 4 layers. The cut appears through all 4 layers.
medium.explanation: Two folds create two lines of symmetry, and the single cut is reflected across both fold lines, producing 4 copies.

hard.question: Ritu makes two paper aeroplanes. One has both wings exactly the same size. The other has one wing longer than the other. Which aeroplane will fly straighter and why? What does this tell us about the importance of symmetry?
hard.answer: The aeroplane with equal wings will fly straighter and farther. The unequal-wing plane will tilt and spin because one wing pushes more air than the other. Symmetry creates balance, and balance leads to steady, predictable movement. This is why real aeroplanes are designed symmetrically.
hard.explanation: Equal wings produce equal lift on both sides, keeping the plane balanced. Unequal wings cause uneven forces.

hard.question: You start with a square tile. You cut a zigzag piece from the left side and tape it to the right side. Can this new shape still tile a flat surface without gaps? Explain why.
hard.answer: Yes! The new shape can still tile. The zigzag taken from the left side of one tile fits perfectly into the zigzag space on the left side of the tile next to it. Since the removed piece and the added piece are identical, the tiles still lock together with no gaps and no overlaps.
hard.explanation: Cutting from one side and adding the same piece to the opposite side preserves the tiling property because the shapes interlock.
